title: Judges Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who came up from Gilgal to Bochim to speak to the children of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: An angel of the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 2:1 states that an angel of the LORD came up from Gilgal to Bochim to speak to the children of Israel.

questions.question: What did the angel of the LORD remind Israel that He had sworn to their fathers?
options: To make them rulers of the world
questions.correctAnswer: To never break His covenant
questions.explanation: Judges 2:1 explains that the angel said God had sworn to their fathers that He would never break His covenant with them.

questions.question: What were the Israelites commanded NOT to make with the inhabitants of the land?
questions.correctAnswer: No league
questions.explanation: Judges 2:2 commands that the Israelites shall make no league with the inhabitants of the land.

questions.question: What were the Israelites supposed to do to the altars of the inhabitants of the land?
questions.correctAnswer: Throw them down
questions.explanation: Judges 2:2 instructs the Israelites to throw down the altars of the inhabitants of the land.

questions.question: Why did the LORD say He would not drive out the inhabitants from before Israel?
options: Because the inhabitants were His chosen people
questions.correctAnswer: Because they disobeyed His voice
questions.explanation: Judges 2:3 says that because Israel had not obeyed God's voice, He would not drive out the inhabitants, but they would be thorns and snares to Israel.

questions.question: What did the people of Israel do when the angel of the LORD spoke to them?
options: Lifted up their voice, and wept
questions.correctAnswer: Lifted up their voice, and wept
questions.explanation: Judges 2:4 records that when the angel spoke, the people lifted up their voice and wept.

questions.question: What name did the people give to the place where the angel spoke to them?
questions.correctAnswer: Bochim
questions.explanation: Judges 2:5 states that the people called the place Bochim after the angel spoke to them.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do at Bochim after the angel's message?
options: Made a covenant with the land's inhabitants
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrificed unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 2:5 tells us they sacrificed there unto the LORD at Bochim.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel do after Joshua let them go?
options: Each went unto his inheritance to possess the land
questions.correctAnswer: Each went unto his inheritance to possess the land
questions.explanation: Judges 2:6 says that after Joshua let the people go, each man went to his inheritance to possess the land.

questions.question: How long did the people serve the LORD according to Judges 2:7?
options: All the days of Joshua and the elders that outlived him
Until they made a new king
questions.correctAnswer: All the days of Joshua and the elders that outlived him
questions.explanation: Judges 2:7 confirms that the people served the LORD all the days of Joshua and the elders who outlived him.

questions.question: How old was Joshua when he died?
options: One hundred and ten years old
One hundred and twenty years old
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred and ten years old
questions.explanation: Judges 2:8 states Joshua died at the age of 110.

questions.question: Where was Joshua buried?
options: In the border of his inheritance in Timnathheres
questions.correctAnswer: In the border of his inheritance in Timnathheres
questions.explanation: Judges 2:9 tells us Joshua was buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnathheres, in the mount of Ephraim.

questions.question: True or False: The generation after Joshua knew the LORD and His works for Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 2:10 states that the generation after Joshua did not know the LORD nor the works He had done for Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel served Baalim after Joshua’s generation.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 2:11 clearly says the children of Israel did evil and served Baalim.

questions.question: In Judges 2, which event came first?
options: The angel of the LORD spoke to Israel at Bochim
Israelites went to possess their inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: The angel of the LORD spoke to Israel at Bochim
questions.explanation: Judges 2:1-5 shows that the angel's visit to Bochim happened before Joshua’s death (verse 8) and before Israelites served Baalim (verse 11) or went to possess their inheritance (verse 6).

medium.title: Judges Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Where was Joshua buried according to Judges 2?
options: In the border of his inheritance in Timnathheres, in the mount of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: In the border of his inheritance in Timnathheres, in the mount of Ephraim
questions.explanation: Judges 2:9 states that Joshua was buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnathheres, in the mount of Ephraim, on the north side of the hill Gaash.

questions.question: What characterized the generation that arose after those who knew the LORD and His works?
options: They knew not the LORD nor the works He had done for Israel
They built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They knew not the LORD nor the works He had done for Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 2:10 explains that a new generation arose after the previous one, which did not know the LORD nor the works He had done for Israel.

questions.question: According to Judges 2, what did the children of Israel do that was evil in the sight of the LORD?
options: They built new altars to the LORD
They destroyed the idols of the other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They served Baalim
questions.explanation: Judges 2:11 states that the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD and served Baalim.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do that provoked the LORD to anger as described in Judges 2?
options: Forsook the LORD God of their fathers and followed other gods
questions.correctAnswer: Forsook the LORD God of their fathers and followed other gods
questions.explanation: Judges 2:12 tells that they forsook the LORD God of their fathers and followed other gods, provoking the LORD to anger.

questions.question: Which gods did the Israelites serve after forsaking the LORD, according to Judges 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Baal and Ashtaroth
questions.explanation: Judges 2:13 specifies that after forsaking the LORD, they served Baal and Ashtaroth.

questions.question: What consequence did Israel face because of their disobedience and serving other gods?
options: The LORD delivered them into the hands of spoilers and enemies
They were blessed with peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD delivered them into the hands of spoilers and enemies
questions.explanation: Judges 2:14 explains that the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and He delivered them into the hands of spoilers and enemies so they could no longer stand before them.

questions.question: How does Judges 2 describe the LORD's hand upon Israel as they went out?
options: The hand of the LORD was against them for evil
The hand of the LORD was to protect them
The hand of the LORD was neutral
The hand of the LORD was to bless their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The hand of the LORD was against them for evil
questions.explanation: Judges 2:15 states that wherever Israel went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for evil, fulfilling His word and oath, and they were greatly distressed.

questions.question: What did the LORD do to help Israel despite their disobedience?
options: Raised up judges who delivered them from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Raised up judges who delivered them from their enemies
questions.explanation: Judges 2:16 states that the LORD raised up judges who delivered Israel out of the hand of those that spoiled them.

questions.question: How does Judges 2 teach us about God's response to repentance and deliverance?
options: God was with the judge and delivered Israel because He repented of their groanings
God punished Israel without delivering them
God only delivered Israel after they fully obeyed
questions.correctAnswer: God was with the judge and delivered Israel because He repented of their groanings
questions.explanation: Judges 2:18 explains that when the LORD raised up judges, He was with them and delivered Israel because He was moved to pity by their groaning under oppression.

questions.question: What pattern of behavior did Israel exhibit after the death of their judges?
options: They returned to corruption and served other gods more than their fathers
They became more faithful to the LORD
They built new altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They returned to corruption and served other gods more than their fathers
questions.explanation: Judges 2:19 tells that after the judge died, Israel corrupted themselves more than their fathers and continued to serve other gods.

questions.question: According to Judges 2, why did the LORD not drive out certain nations left in the land after Joshua’s death?
options: To prove whether Israel would obey His ways
questions.correctAnswer: To prove whether Israel would obey His ways
questions.explanation: Judges 2:22 explains that the LORD left those nations to prove Israel whether they would keep the way of the LORD as their fathers did.

questions.question: What is the connection between Israel’s transgression of the covenant and the LORD’s decision about the remaining nations?
options: Because Israel transgressed, the LORD would not drive out the remaining nations hastily
Because Israel was faithful, the LORD drove out all nations quickly
The LORD immediately destroyed all remaining nations regardless
Israel’s faithfulness caused the LORD to delay judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Because Israel transgressed, the LORD would not drive out the remaining nations hastily
questions.explanation: Judges 2:20-23 show that because Israel transgressed the covenant and did not listen to the LORD, He left the nations and did not drive them out quickly, as a test of Israel’s faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 2, all generations after Joshua fully knew the LORD and served Him faithfully.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 2:10 states that a generation arose after those who knew the LORD which did not know Him or His works, indicating unfaithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD’s anger against Israel led Him to deliver them into the hands of their enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 2:14 records that the LORD’s anger was hot against Israel and He delivered them into the hands of spoilers and enemies as a consequence.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 2 teaches that Israel's obedience guaranteed that the LORD would not allow enemies to oppress them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 2:15-16 show that despite warnings, Israel was oppressed because of disobedience, but the LORD raised judges to deliver them, indicating obedience was necessary but not always immediately resulting in peace.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Judges 2:17, what did the Israelites do after being delivered by their judges?
options: They remained faithful to the LORD
They quickly turned to other gods and disobeyed the commandments
They built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They quickly turned to other gods and disobeyed the commandments
questions.explanation: Judges 2:17 states that the Israelites did not obey their judges but went a whoring after other gods and quickly turned out of the way which their fathers walked in, disobeying the commandments of the LORD.

questions.question: What reason does Judges 2:18 give for the LORD delivering Israel through judges?
options: Because the judges were powerful warriors
Because the LORD repented due to their groanings under oppression
Because the judges made covenants with Israel's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD repented due to their groanings under oppression
questions.explanation: Judges 2:18 explains that the LORD was with the judges and delivered Israel for all the days of the judge because the LORD repented due to the groanings of Israel under their oppressors.

questions.question: What happened after the death of each judge according to Judges 2:19?
options: Israel became more faithful than before
Israel corrupted themselves more and followed other gods
Israel built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Israel corrupted themselves more and followed other gods
questions.explanation: Judges 2:19 states that after each judge died, Israel returned to corrupt themselves more than their fathers by following other gods and ceasing not from their stubborn ways.

questions.question: Why was the anger of the LORD hot against Israel according to Judges 2:20?
options: Because they built altars to the LORD
Because they transgressed the covenant and did not heed God's voice
questions.correctAnswer: Because they transgressed the covenant and did not heed God's voice
questions.explanation: Judges 2:20 says the LORD's anger was hot because Israel had transgressed the covenant commanded to their fathers and had not hearkened unto His voice.

questions.question: According to Judges 2:21, what did the LORD decide about driving out the nations Joshua left?
options: He would drive them out immediately
He would not drive them out henceforth
He would destroy Israel for their disobedience
He would send prophets to warn Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He would not drive them out henceforth
questions.explanation: Judges 2:21 states the LORD decided not to drive out any of the nations which Joshua left when he died.

questions.question: What was the purpose of leaving the nations in the land according to Judges 2:22?
options: To prove Israel whether they would keep the LORD's ways
To encourage Israel to build their temples
questions.correctAnswer: To prove Israel whether they would keep the LORD's ways
questions.explanation: Judges 2:22 explains that the LORD left the nations to prove Israel whether they would keep the way of the LORD to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Judges 2:23's explanation of the LORD's actions towards the nations Joshua did not drive out?
options: Inclusio, framing the narrative with repeated themes
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism emphasizing the LORD's patience
questions.explanation: Judges 2:23 uses parallel phrases ('without driving them out hastily; neither delivered he them into the hand of Joshua') to emphasize the LORD's deliberate patience, a literary device known as parallelism.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of Israel's repeated disobedience and God's raising judges found in Judges 2:18?
questions.explanation: Psalm 106:34-43 recounts Israel's repeated sins and God's mercy in raising leaders to deliver them, echoing the cycle described in Judges 2:18.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'whoring' in Judges 2:17 imply in the original context?
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry and unfaithfulness to God
questions.explanation: In Judges 2:17, the Hebrew term translated as 'whoring' metaphorically refers to spiritual unfaithfulness and idolatry, representing Israel's turning away from God to serve other gods.

questions.question: Judges 2:16 mentions the LORD raising up judges. What was the primary role of these judges?
options: To lead Israel in building the temple
To deliver Israel from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: To deliver Israel from their enemies
questions.explanation: Judges 2:16 states the LORD raised judges who delivered Israel out of the hands of those that spoiled them, highlighting their role as deliverers.

questions.question: What was the consequence for Israel as described in Judges 2:14 when the LORD's anger was hot against them?
options: They were delivered into the hands of spoilers and enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They were delivered into the hands of spoilers and enemies
questions.explanation: Judges 2:14 explains that because of the LORD's anger, Israel was delivered into the hands of spoilers and enemies who oppressed them severely.

questions.question: According to Judges 2:10, what distinguished the new generation of Israelites from their fathers?
options: They were more faithful to God
They did not know the LORD nor His works for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They did not know the LORD nor His works for Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 2:10 states that the new generation arose after the former died, and this generation knew not the LORD nor the works He had done for Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 2:7 states that the people served the LORD only during Joshua’s lifetime.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 2:7 says the people served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, not just during Joshua's lifetime.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 2:22 indicates that the LORD used the remaining nations to test Israel's faithfulness to His covenant.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 2:22 explicitly states that the LORD left the nations to prove Israel whether they would keep the way of the LORD as their fathers did.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a covenant similar to the one referenced in Judges 2:1 where God promises never to break it?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis (God's covenant with Abraham)
questions.explanation: Judges 2:1 references God's covenant with their fathers, which connects to the Abrahamic covenant in Genesis 15:18 where God swears to give the land to Abraham's descendants.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God's statement in Judges 2:1 that He will "never break my covenant with you"?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Judges 2:1 shows God's immutability because He declares His covenant to the fathers will never be broken, indicating His unchanging faithfulness. This reflects God's consistent and unalterable nature (Malachi 3:6).

questions.question: According to Judges 2:2, what specific command did God give the Israelites regarding their relationship with the inhabitants of the land?
options: Make no league and throw down their altars
Ignore the inhabitants and build their own altars
Worship the gods of the inhabitants
questions.correctAnswer: Make no league and throw down their altars
questions.explanation: Judges 2:2 commands Israel to make no league with the inhabitants and to throw down their altars, emphasizing God's call for separation from idolatry and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What theological principle is illustrated by God allowing the nations to remain as 'thorns in your sides' in Judges 2:3?
options: The sovereignty of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment as corrective discipline
questions.explanation: Judges 2:3 reveals that God permits enemies as thorns in Israel's sides, illustrating His use of judgment as discipline to correct and test His people’s faithfulness (Hebrews 12:6).

questions.question: What does Judges 2:7 reveal about the faithfulness of the generation who lived during Joshua's leadership?
options: They served the LORD all their days
They quickly turned to other gods
They were indifferent to God's works
questions.correctAnswer: They served the LORD all their days
questions.explanation: Judges 2:7 states that the people served the LORD during Joshua’s lifetime and the days of the elders who witnessed God's works, showing a faithful generation that honored God’s deeds.

questions.question: How does Judges 2:10 contribute to the doctrine of corporate generational covenant responsibility?
options: A new generation arose that knew not the LORD nor His works
All generations equally remember God's works
Generations have no impact on covenant relationship
questions.correctAnswer: A new generation arose that knew not the LORD nor His works
questions.explanation: Judges 2:10 highlights the failure of a subsequent generation to know God or His works, underscoring corporate generational responsibility in maintaining covenant faithfulness (Deuteronomy 6:6-7).

questions.question: What is the primary theological reason for Israel's defeat and oppression as described in Judges 2:14?
options: God’s anger because of their idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: God’s anger because of their idolatry
questions.explanation: Judges 2:14 teaches that Israel’s oppression is due to the LORD’s anger against their idolatry and abandonment of Him, showing divine justice in response to sin (Romans 1:18).

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by the cycle of sin, judgment, deliverance, and relapse described from Judges 2:16 to 2:19?
options: The cyclical nature of human sin and divine mercy
questions.correctAnswer: The cyclical nature of human sin and divine mercy
questions.explanation: Judges 2:16-19 depicts repeated cycles of Israel’s sin, God raising judges to deliver, and Israel’s relapse, illustrating human fallenness and God's patient mercy (Psalm 103:8).

questions.question: How does Judges 2:18 demonstrate the attribute of God’s mercy despite Israel’s repeated sin?
options: God repents and delivers Israel when they groan
questions.correctAnswer: God repents and delivers Israel when they groan
questions.explanation: Judges 2:18 shows God’s mercy as He delivers Israel through judges because He repents or relents in response to their groaning, revealing compassion despite their rebellion (Exodus 32:14).

questions.question: What combined theological teaching emerges from Judges 2:20-22 about God’s permissive will and testing of Israel?
options: God allows remaining nations to test Israel's faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God allows remaining nations to test Israel's faithfulness
questions.explanation: Judges 2:20-22 teaches that God’s wrath leads Him to not drive out all nations, permitting them to remain as a test of Israel’s obedience, showing God’s sovereign permissive will for refinement (Deuteronomy 8:2).

questions.question: How does Judges 2:6-9 narrate the transition of leadership and its theological significance for Israel’s possession of the land?
options: Joshua dies before the conquest begins
Joshua’s death marks the end of an era of direct obedience
Leadership passes to the elders who outlive Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua’s death marks the end of an era of direct obedience
questions.explanation: Judges 2:6-9 recounts Joshua’s death after the land possession and notes the elders who served the LORD, signifying a transition from divinely guided conquest to a new phase where faithfulness is tested.

questions.question: What apologetic challenge does Judges 2:14-15 address regarding the justice of God in allowing Israel to be oppressed by enemies?
options: Why does God allow evil to flourish?
Why does God not punish Israel’s enemies?
Why does God immediately deliver Israel every time?
Why does God forbid alliances with nations?
questions.correctAnswer: Why does God allow evil to flourish?
questions.explanation: Judges 2:14-15 responds to sceptics questioning God’s justice by showing that Israel’s oppression is a just consequence of their sin, demonstrating God’s righteous judgment rather than neglect (Romans 1:18).

questions.question: What does the naming of the place 'Bochim' in Judges 2:5 signify theologically about Israel's response to divine rebuke?
questions.correctAnswer: Repentant weeping and sacrifice
questions.explanation: Judges 2:5 shows Israel named the place Bochim, meaning 'weepers,' after hearing the angel’s rebuke and responding with weeping and sacrifice, indicating a repentant heart before God.

questions.question: What does Judges 2:12-13 reveal about the nature of apostasy among the Israelites?
options: They abandoned the LORD and served foreign gods like Baal and Ashtaroth
They strengthened their faith in the LORD
They remained neutral in religious matters
They sought to unify all gods
questions.correctAnswer: They abandoned the LORD and served foreign gods like Baal and Ashtaroth
questions.explanation: Judges 2:12-13 describes Israel’s apostasy as forsaking the LORD and serving Baal and Ashtaroth, demonstrating the seriousness of idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Judges 2:23 connect the narrative of Judges to the broader redemptive storyline of Israel's covenant testing?
options: God delays driving out nations to test Israel’s obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God delays driving out nations to test Israel’s obedience
questions.explanation: Judges 2:23 concludes that God did not swiftly deliver all nations but left them to test Israel’s faithfulness, fitting within the redemptive theme of covenant testing and reliance on God (Deuteronomy 8:16).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's justice and mercy is synthesized from Judges 2:14 and Judges 2:18?
options: God is only merciful and never just
God’s anger brings judgment, but His mercy raises deliverers
questions.correctAnswer: God’s anger brings judgment, but His mercy raises deliverers
questions.explanation: Judges 2:14 shows God’s anger bringing judgment through enemies, while Judges 2:18 shows God's mercy raising judges to deliver Israel, demonstrating a balance of justice and mercy.
